statements.t: "Q3 was a milestone quarter — we exceeded the top end of our guidance across all key metrics for the sixth consecutive quarter, delivered positive GAAP earnings per share for the first time since our IPO, and reached our net leverage milestone a quarter ahead of plan," said Jim Peck, Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer.
We're raising our full year 2026 guidance to reflect Q3 outperformance, and we expect further strengthening in 2027."

• Ongoing integration of advanced technology, including AI, continues to support the Company's 2026 Restructuring Program, which remains on track to deliver anticipated annualized cost savings of approximately $70 million to $80 million (refer to "2026 Restructuring Program" discussion below)
The Company's Net Leverage Ratio was 2.9x at September 30, 2026, down from 3.1x at June 30, 2026 and 4.6x at the time of the IPO, achieving the Company's sub-3.0x target one quarter ahead of plan.
In February 2026, the Company approved an incremental cost realignment program (the "2026 Program") intended to further streamline the organization and drive operational efficiency.

Investments in automation and artificial intelligence ("AI") are anticipated to accelerate the Company’s optimization efforts as it begins its journey to operationalize these digital tools throughout the organization.

The Company expects to incur total pre-tax restructuring charges related to the 2026 Program of approximately $65 million to $75 million, the substantial majority of which would result in cash expenditures.

As of year-to-date fiscal 2026, the Company has incurred substantially all of the restructuring charges associated with the 2026 Program, and expects the balance to be incurred in the fourth quarter of 2026 and first half of 2027.
Our outlook is based on a number of assumptions that are subject to change, many of which are outside of the control of the Company.
There can be no assurance that the Company will achieve the results expressed by this guidance.
Annualized Revenue is not a forecast and the active contracts at the end of a reporting period used in calculating Annualized Revenue may or may not be extended or renewed by our clients.

We are not able to provide, without unreasonable effort, a reconciliation of the guidance for these measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measure because we do not currently have sufficient data to accurately estimate the variables and individual adjustments included in the most directly comparable GAAP measure that would be necessary for such reconciliations, including (a) costs related to potential debt…

Therefore, because our management cannot estimate on a forward-looking basis without unreasonable effort the impact these variables and individual adjustments will have on its reported results in accordance with GAAP, it is unable to provide a reconciliation of the non-GAAP financial measures included in its fourth quarter and full year 2026 guidance.
